Recurrent aphthous stomatitis

Randomized studies generally report reduced pain or faster healing, though study size and outcome timing limit confidence.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Randomized studies generally report reduced pain or faster healing, though study size and outcome timing limit confidence.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact aphthous-stomatitis category contains 44 unique titles: 18 human randomized reports, 13 additional human reports such as nonrandomized studies, case reports, and series, 11 reviews or syntheses, and one animal-tagged and one in-vitro record. Reviews overlap primary trials, and some reports may evaluate different lesion types or treatment timing. (AlHerafi et al. 2024)

Human and clinical evidence

The 2024 randomized trial included 64 patients assigned to 808 nm, 660 nm, 635 nm, or placebo groups. It reported improvement in pain and lesion measures, with pain reaching zero by day seven in active groups and the strongest lesion-size signal in the 808 nm arm at selected times. The one-month follow-up did not identify a recurrence difference. The trial remains small, and its selected short-term results require replication.

Animal evidence

One animal-tagged publication appears in the exact category. The clinical literature remains the principal evidence base, and the animal record should not be combined with patient outcomes.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

One in-vitro record is indexed, likely addressing biological mechanisms rather than pain or healing in patients. It does not add an independent clinical cohort.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The cited trial compared 635 nm and 660 nm visible red light with 808 nm near-infrared light. Other records vary in device, fluence, contact technique, number of points, and whether treatment is repeated. Exact settings not reported in the database are not inferred.

Interpretation

Small randomized studies have reported lower pain or faster healing, including reductions in pain and lesion severity at selected times in a recent trial. The one-month follow-up did not identify a recurrence difference. Results vary across wavelengths, protocols, and follow-up periods, so larger sham-controlled studies are needed.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term pain or lesion healing Very low for recurrence reduction

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The category contains 44 unique titles, including 18 randomized human reports and 11 reviews or syntheses. Lesion size, treatment wavelength, comparator, and timing vary. A recent four-arm study reported reduced pain and lesion severity, but evidence needs larger trials with standardized recurrence and healing outcomes.
